P is fixed solely as the product of rate-one exponential measures and does not depend on V,alpha,beta,eta,y,r or z0; epsilon is the fixed coordinatewise nonnegative-part map. c and Phi depend on eta,V,y,r; S depends on V,r; rate depends on eta,V,r; Lambda,tau,next,record and eventTime inherit the displayed dependence on eta,V,y,r and their state/threshold/sequence inputs. alpha and beta enter only through the hypotheses and the allowed choice of the witness, not as explicit arguments in the literal dynamical formulas. The witness Z can depend on all outer data E,V,alpha,beta,eta and the hypothesis witnesses; its displayed arguments are y,r,z0,t,sample, and it is chosen once for all of them. The P-null exceptional set allowed in (D) can depend on fixed y,r,z0 and on outer data, but not on t, because every t lies inside the same almost-everywhere assertion. The witnesses n and a in (D) may depend on y,r,z0,sample,t. All explicit numerical constants are fixed: exponential rate 1, initial/hitting-start time 0, reflection multiplier 2, and step restriction upper bound 1. No unspecified finite bound, universal constant, asymptotic constant, expected-cost constant or dimension-dependent estimate is asserted.
scopes_senses: The analytic assumptions are pointwise; the measurability and the two conditional rules (B),(C) are global assertions, with (B),(C) applying to every real sequence, not merely P-almost every one. Only (D) is almost everywhere, for each fixed parameter triple; its universal time quantifier lies inside that almost-everywhere quantifier, so it is stronger than a separate almost-everywhere assertion for each time. The bracketing is inclusive at eventTime(n) and strictly exclusive at eventTime(n+1); the local inequality in (D) is also strict. Subtraction t-u in NNReal is truncated to max(t-u,0); (D) explicitly ensures u<=t. Comparisons of finite times to eventTime use their WithTop casts. The stopped record has eventTime infinity, is absorbing under next, and has no state at infinity; no finite-state update is made when tau=infinity. untopD 0 returns the finite value, or zero at infinity, but the update is guarded before its use in the finite branch. tau is defined as a hit-set infimum and the definition alone is not an extra assertion that the infimum is attained. Nonpositive sample coordinates give epsilon=0; the definitions remain total and can allow zero waiting increments. The pointwise fallback rule covers any time for which no bracket exists, including exceptional sampling behavior; the assertion of a bracket for every time belongs to (D). The reflection coefficient uses total real division: when g(q)-g(r)=0, division by its squared norm is division by zero in Lean (equal to zero), so S leaves the state unchanged. eta>0 makes sqrt(eta)>0, so the flow's sqrt denominator is nonzero under the hypotheses. Lambda is the ordinary real interval integral evaluated at the finite nonnegative endpoint; no integral to infinity is in the statement. Gradient, Frechet derivatives, trigonometric operations and square root have their literal real/inner-product meanings. Equality of Z at time zero is explicitly asserted in (D), within its almost-everywhere scope; the text does not separately assert this equality pointwise for every sample. Nothing in the displayed proposition requires uniqueness of Z, uniqueness of the bracket index or state witness, or a common full-measure set for all y,r,z0.
